human_reorganization: Hilbert--Schmidt tensors identify the closed linear Gaussian field space. The finite fourth-moment computation gives the formal completed energy/projection identity in conventional notation; no additional formal tensor theorem is claimed.
The cutoff error estimate follows from the exact orthogonal energy and the bounded completed divergence restriction.
The inverse-number recovery norm estimate is the classical orthogonal-chaos argument on a probability space generated by the isonormal family; no extraneous non-Gaussian factor is permitted.

The abstract presentation uses an arbitrary orthonormal output family in the same source Hilbert space. Frozen forcing uses its specific coordinate basis. No alignment with the Brownian input directions is added.

The generic right-inverse obstruction is reconstructed from adjointness, expectation and an infinite first-chaos left inverse. Compactness concerns the full observation operator, not a particular trace-admitted field.

The deterministic scalar synthesis T_t on ell2 is distinct from a unit-amplitude Hilbert-valued random forcing field. For linear rates it is compact by finite-rank norm approximation but not Hilbert-Schmidt at positive time. The displayed sharper tail bound [2(N+1)]^(-1/2) is an elementary human deduction; the source sufficient bound is (N+1)^(-1/2).

The monic Wick convention includes u^d/d! in its generating function. Exact covariance d! inner(h,k)^d yields the orthogonal-series criterion. The paper reconstructs the original closed-gradient domain and adjoint recovery through finite product rules and simultaneous graph convergence, rather than positing a new derivative.

The formal actual harmonic-weighted Brownian centered-square series converges while its raw-square means diverge. A separate unit-coefficient exponential Wick series at linear rates converges for each integer d>=2 by a direct stated instantiation of the general criterion, not a separately named formal positive-time theorem. It is a scalar observable and does not construct the missing first-chaos Hilbert field or an SPDE solution.

Full modal Brownian past, including every earlier time and every mode, gives exact conditional Wick prediction. The norm and increment identity are proved by Gaussian independent increments and L2 completion. Initial t^(d/2) norm scaling is separate from positive-time square-root increment scaling. The formal harmonic quadratic example refutes every squared-increment exponent alpha>1 near time one half; no almost-sure optimal regularity is claimed.

Section 9 realizes integer entrywise covariance powers by normalized actual Wick polynomials. Positive semidefiniteness follows directly from a genuine finite L2 energy. Fractional Wick Gram identities are not interpreted as a fractional-time generator or as activation of the queued Hermite-process campaign.

Actual independent modal Brownian motions give a normalized degree-q Wick martingale and a Gaussian deterministic time-change with the same min(s,t)^q covariance. At q=2 their fourth moments are 15t^4 and 3t^4; the Wick increment has conditional second moment 2h B_s^2+h^2, also after conditioning on its own past, while the Gaussian time-change has independent increments. These complete classical law/conditional-variance computations are labelled human deductions, not new formal theorem names.

Finite Brownian entrywise covariance-power matrices factor as L diag((j+1)^k-j^k) L-transpose. Actual difference vectors give generalized eigenvalues d_k(j)/d_l(j), including 7/3 rather than 7. Congruence gives the printed sharp Loewner comparisons as explicit human classical deductions. Ordinary matrix powers remain different.

The existing primary Baudoin chaos context is retained. No new Gaussian covariance theorem, temporal generator, independence principle, curvature correspondence, SPDE existence or scale-uniform estimate is claimed.

Section 10 divides the monic Wick fields by sqrt(q!) and therefore divides the source squared metric bounds by q!. The positive-correlation and unit-source assumptions are explicit; equal-variance quadratic folding is not a global embedding.

The actual normalized fractional directions exclude time zero. The compact positive-time interval calculation using the mean value theorem and the exact normalized covariance proves matching squared increment exponent 2H as a labelled human deduction. No optimal sample-path exponent, Hermite-process identification or Markov generator follows.

Section 7.1 proves the actual completed-observation conditional Wick formula by orthogonal Gaussian splitting, full generated-sigma-algebra independence and locally dominated L2 differentiation. The projected variance is used in its Wick subtraction.

Countable predicted sums converge through the bounded conditional projection of the original orthogonal series. The displayed finite double Gram sums converge in squared norm; no absolute infinite double-sum or preserved mode orthogonality is assumed. The inverse-degree recovery energy is a human consequence of the same homogeneous-chaos spectral identity already printed.

The two-mode sum/difference calibration shows why deleting projected Gram cross terms fails. The actual two Brownian unit-time quadratic modes have predicted sum energy two. These are classical exact observation identities, not nonlinear SPDE or independence claims.

Section 11 separates the one-mode temporal threshold alpha>1/2 from the infinite-mode reciprocal-rate trace condition. The actual zero-generator Riemann-Liouville response has exact variance t^(2 alpha-1)/(Gamma(alpha)^2(2 alpha-1)), original Gaussian-source derivative and sharp initial variance exponent. Explicit cutoff-energy divergence at and below alpha=1/2 and the covariance asymptotic distinguishing unit-variance Liouville motion from standard fBM for H unequal to 1/2 are labelled classical human deductions. Neither a Mittag-Leffler resolvent, physical-time derivative nor a new stochastic PDE solution is asserted.

Section 12 reconstructs exact scalar deterministic-multiplier covariance, increment and approximation-error identities in the original Gaussian L2 space, with the same original closed Gaussian derivative. The threshold converse explicitly retains 0<m<=|g|<=M globally. Sharp supremum-to-L2 operator norm and uniform-on-bounded-time mean-square norm convergence are labelled elementary human deductions of the mapped bound; expected suprema, path convergence and random-coefficient integration are not inferred. Four principal modules were read fully, while only their relevant scalar declarations are mapped.

The exponential Volterra calibration proves exact full-terminal Markov prediction in the original natural past by orthogonal Gaussian innovation and the finite-cylinder monotone-class passage. The strictly positive L2 martingale defect at positive damping is retained. Its integrating-factor martingale has the actual deterministic Ito coefficient exp(lambda u). A separate complete Bochner profile/Fubini calculation gives Y_t=B_t-lambda integral_0^t Y_r dr in the original Gaussian L2 space, with continuous drift derivative and exact nonzero derivative energy. Zero damping is treated directly. These classical OU mechanisms supply no all-path simultaneous semimartingale identity or random-kernel stochastic Fubini theorem and are not transferred to arbitrary fractional Volterra kernels.
